In 2006, my father had a stroke which gaming-wise rendered his left hand useless. He was a fan of FPS games, which obviously he cant play. Any suggested controllers/ways to play?

Does your father have enough mobility in his left arm to push the spacebar? He can probably play ROMs for those arcade on-rails shooters. If they made the games work with just a gun and a foot pedal, I'm sure it can be played with a mouse and a spacebar.

There are lots of guides out there on how to modify existing controllers (modifying them to be controllable with one hand specifically, in fact), and quite a few people willing to build custom controllers for a fee.

Had a buddy who lost a thumb to an industrial accident. His solution was a flightstick with a hat. That gave him 2 analog inputs, one from the stick and one from the hat. He was actually quite a badass at fps still.
Altitude is a really fun PC game that you can play one handed with just the mouse.

America's Election Watchdogs Are Literally Arguing Over Whether FEC Commissioners Are People

Funny article. But it's not unreasonable to argue that the rules governing how the commission deals with lobbying by members of the public don't apply to members of a commission themselves. It's a problem if the commission exists to respond to public complaints but the only "members of the public" complaining about an issue are the commissioners themselves. In that case they cease to be a body that responds to public concerns and become a free-standing body that both invents the issues it'll rule on and then decides how to rule. Judges don't get to file suit in their own courts and then sit as both petitioner and judge at the same time.

Presumably if the particular issue being raised is one of public concern some actual member of the public can raise it.
